grammar_concept.title: Present Perfect for Life Experiences
grammar_concept.rule: Use "have/has + past participle" to talk about experiences at an unspecified time in your life — the exact when doesn't matter, only that it happened (or hasn't).
grammar_concept.simple_explanation: This is different from the Past Simple: Past Simple needs a specific time (yesterday, in 2019); Present Perfect for experience deliberately does NOT give one — it's about your life up to now, as a whole.
grammar_concept.example: I have visited Paris twice. She has never eaten sushi. Have you ever worked abroad?
grammar_concept.example_translation: Já visitei Paris duas vezes. Ela nunca comeu sushi. Já alguma vez trabalhaste no estrangeiro?
grammar_concept.common_mistake_pt: Português não tem um tempo verbal equivalente para esta ideia específica — "já visitei" tanto pode ser Present Perfect como Past Simple em inglês, dependendo do contexto. Falantes de português tendem a usar sempre Past Simple ("I visited Paris") mesmo quando a ideia é "alguma vez na vida", não um momento específico, e a esquecer o particípio passado correto de verbos irregulares ("I have eated" em vez de "I have eaten").
grammar_concept.correction: Se há uma data ou momento específico (yesterday, last year, in 2019), use Past Simple. Se a pergunta é "alguma vez na tua vida", sem data nenhuma, use Present Perfect: have/has + particípio passado (go→gone, eat→eaten, see→seen).
grammar_concept.real_world_example: Numa entrevista de emprego: "Have you ever managed a team before?" — "Yes, I've managed a team of five people at my last job."

vocabulary.definition_en: used with Present Perfect to say something has not happened at any point in your life
example_sentences: I have never been to Japan.

vocabulary.definition_en: used to ask if someone has had a particular experience at any point in their life
example_sentences: Have you ever tried Thai food?
So far, I have read three books this year.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: I ___ never ___ (be) to Australia.
exercises.explanation: "I" usa "have" (não "has"), e o particípio passado de "be" é "been".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Confundir o particípio passado "been" com o infinitivo "be" é muito comum.

correct_answer: She has visited Paris three times.
distractors: She has visit Paris three times.
She have visited Paris three times.
She visited Paris three times ago.
exercises.explanation: "She" usa "has" + particípio passado ("visited") — sem data específica, é experiência de vida.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar "have" em vez de "has" com a 3ª pessoa do singular é o erro mais comum.

correct_answer: to ask if someone has had a particular experience at any point in their life
distractors: to ask what someone did yesterday
to ask about someone's future plans
exercises.explanation: "Have you ever...?" pergunta sobre experiência de vida, sem data específica.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the audio. What has Carla never done?
exercises.explanation: No áudio, ouve-se: "Carla has travelled a lot, but she has never ridden a horse."
exercises.transcript: Carla has travelled a lot, but she has never ridden a horse.

exercises.prompt: Read the text: "Marco has lived in three different countries. So far, he has learned two new languages and made friends all over the world." How many languages has Marco learned so far?
exercises.explanation: O texto diz diretamente "he has learned two new languages".

exercises.prompt: Translate to English: "Já alguma vez trabalhaste no estrangeiro?"
exercises.explanation: "Já alguma vez...?" sem data específica corresponde a Present Perfect: "Have you ever...?".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Traduzir diretamente com Past Simple ("Did you work abroad?") perde a nuance de "alguma vez na vida".

steps.content: "Have" in fast, natural speech is often reduced to /əv/ or even just /v/ — "I've been", "She's visited" — listen for this contracted form, you will hear it constantly from native speakers.

steps.prompt: Talk about 3 things you have never done, using "I have never...".
Write 5 sentences about your life experiences using the Present Perfect (have you visited, tried, learned...).
